anchors_verified.A3_note: DRIFT: expect was 57, pre-work measured 80, post-work 81. The drift is this packet's own prose (the new canonical-convention docs and the new nstation_* test/helper names each add the word 'loft'). Recorded, not stretched.

summary: Generalized the landed two-station certified spline-loft arm (BRIDGE-LOFT-FACTS) to N stations under the kernel-CANONICAL convention, entirely in truck123d/src/bd_bridge.rs. Station parameters are the cumulative centroid-to-centroid chord length normalized to [0,1]. The v-direction is the unique global polynomial of degree N-1 interpolating the section control rows for N <= 9, and the natural C2 cubic spline (standard banded second-derivative system, M_0 = M_{n-1} = 0) with knots AT the station parameters for N >= 10; both routes emit tensor-Bernstein patches (4 x (N) for the global route, 4 x 4 per v-span for the spline route) submitted one row at a time to the sanctioned binding::volume_facts entry, with the landed Green's-theorem planar end-cap moments added and the brackets summed outward. The u-direction reuses the landed per-section reconstruction (spline_loop_spans: chord-length clamped cubics, exact seam closure) and unifies sections by span matching only; a stack whose spans do not match (the corpus's crease-corner / periodic-section case cannot be unified by knot insertion alone) refuses TYPED with the landed NonCanonicalCarrier refusal, never a tolerance stretch. The bbox and mesh generalize spline_loft_mesh. The two-station path is preserved exactly: for N = 2 the Bernstein collocation solve returns the endpoint controls exactly, so the numerator grid is bit-identical to the landed [ba[k], bb[k]] patch, the caps are unchanged, and the line-loft fast path is untouched. No OCC runs at certify time; the one-time OCC fixtures are diagnostic constants.

method.station_law: v_i = cumulative centroid-to-centroid chord length of the section stack, normalized to [0,1] (station_params; sample_loop3 + centroid3).
method.u_unification: per-span reconstruction reuse + span-index matching; unequal span counts refuse typed (open_smooth_loft). Geometry-preserving: the reconstruction normalizes every recorded span to [0,1], so matched spans share the common u-knot structure without approximation; no flattening, no tolerance.
method.v_interpolation_global: N <= 9: solve the Bernstein collocation system B_j^{N-1}(v_i) b_j = y_i (solve_dense, partial pivoting) for each u-control row; one v-segment of degree N-1.
method.v_interpolation_spline: N >= 10: natural C2 cubic spline via the standard tridiagonal second-derivative system (natural_spline_second_derivs, Thomas algorithm) with knots at v_i; each span's four Bernstein controls from the Hermite/M form.
method.volume: one crate::python::binding::volume_facts call per (u-span, v-segment) tensor-Bernstein patch, weights all 1.0, orientation 1.0; exact expansion brackets summed outward; plus the landed planar end-cap terms (1/3) d A and the winding sign absorption.
method.bbox: N = 2: exact union of the two section-loop AABBs (unchanged). N > 2: exact section-loop AABBs unioned with the canonical surface's control-net AABB (the Bernstein convex-hull enclosure, nstation_control_enclosure). This is a certified enclosure; it is not the exact bivariate surface extremum (that needs a 2x2 critical system, not cubic_roots alone).
method.mesh: spline_loft_mesh generalized: ruled quads between consecutive sampled section loops plus the two end-cap fans (identical bytes to the landed two-station mesh at N = 2).

findings.title: N-station canonical volume is exact and cheap
findings.detail: The 42-station synthetic (the tub's scale, 4 u-spans x 41 v-spans = 164 patches) measures in 315.9 ms in the debug test profile through the full tree_facts path (bbox enclosure + volume). No OCC, no approximation, no tolerance.

findings.title: u-unification is span matching, not literal B-spline knot insertion
findings.detail: The landed reconstruction emits independent power-basis spans normalized to [0,1]; the natural N-station extension is span-index matching. This is geometry-preserving and needs no insertion for equal-span stacks (the corpus's airfoil-family sections all carry the same sample count per edge). Unequal-span stacks (e.g. a crease-corner section with a different edge sample count) refuse typed, which is the packet's stop-condition-2 outcome: new carrier work, not tolerance territory.

findings.title: Natural end conditions chosen for the N >= 10 spline
findings.detail: The packet specifies 'the standard banded second-derivative system' without end conditions. The natural choice (M_0 = M_{n-1} = 0) is the textbook standard and is documented in the code. This is the one convention judgement the packet left open; it is a kernel-canonical choice, not an OCC replication.

findings.title: bbox is a certified enclosure for N > 2, exact for N = 2
findings.detail: Exact bivariate surface extrema need a 2x2 critical system, not cubic_roots alone; the implementation unions the exact section-loop AABBs with the control-net (convex-hull) AABB. This is safe (an enclosure) but over-reports on outward-bulging sections. The packet's required tests do not gate the N-station bbox; the two-station bbox path is byte-identical to the landed arm.

findings.title: clippy baseline is already red
findings.detail: cargo clippy -p truck123d --lib --no-deps -D warnings fails on pre-existing lines (e.g. bd_bridge.rs:588 in span_volume, and the pre-existing min[axis] idiom at 975-976). The added lines use the same idioms as the surrounding file, so they introduce no new lint classes beyond the file's existing style. cargo check --all-targets and cargo fmt are green.

v5_net.note: the landed two-station entries must answer bit-identically
v5_net.n2_argument: For N = 2 the Bernstein collocation matrix is exactly [[1,0],[0,1]], so solve_dense returns the endpoint controls bit-exactly; the numerator grid is [ba[k], bb[k]] as landed, the caps and sign absorption are unchanged, and station_params yields v = [0,1] exactly. The two-station bbox and mesh paths are also the landed ones.
